q: Which finding is a CPAP contraindication in this recap?

opts.why: CPAP drops blood pressure more. Skip it in hypotension or shock.
High pressure is not the CPAP no in this recap. Low pressure is.
Crackles from pulmonary edema are a CPAP picture, not a contraindication.
CHF with edema is why you consider CPAP, if pressure is adequate.

q: How does CPAP move fluid in pulmonary edema in this recap?

opts.why: They exhale against pressure. That back pressure pushes fluid from the alveoli back into the bloodstream.
CPAP is meant to push fluid out of the alveoli, not deeper in.
The fluid goes back into the blood, not out the mouth.
Pleural fluid is effusion, not what CPAP does to alveolar fluid.

q: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea in this recap. How do you position them?

opts.why: PND is dyspnea lying down at night. They sleep upright. Keep them sitting up.
Lying flat spreads fluid over more lung. Do not force them flat.
This recap wants them sitting upright, not prone.
Head-down is not the PND position. Sit them up.

q: Hypoxic COPD patient, short EMS transport. Oxygen in this recap?

opts.why: Short transports: still treat hypoxia. Do not withhold oxygen for hypoxic drive.
Do not withhold oxygen from a hypoxic COPD patient on a short run.
A cannula instead of a non-rebreather is the long-transport option, not a short run.
Medical direction is for long or borderline cases. On a short hypoxic run, give oxygen.

q: When does this recap want epinephrine for an allergic reaction?

opts.why: Anaphylaxis is two or more systems. Then epinephrine IM. One system only: no epi.
One system (often skin) is a mild reaction. Monitor and transport. No epi.
Itch alone is one system. No epinephrine.
You need two or more systems, not any sneeze.

q: Bee stinger still in the skin. How does this recap want it out?

opts.why: Scrape it out with a straight edge. Tweezers can squeeze more venom. The sac can inject for about 20 minutes.

opts.t: Pull it out with tweezers now
opts.why: Avoid tweezers. They can squeeze more venom from the sac.

opts.t: Leave the stinger in the skin
opts.why: Scrape it out. The sac can keep injecting.
Do not squeeze the sac. Scrape with a straight edge.

q: Suspected PE. Why can a non-rebreather leave the saturation low in this recap?

opts.why: Air reaches the alveoli, but the clot blocks blood from getting there, so gas exchange fails.
Air does reach the alveoli. Blood does not.
This recap’s PE has adequate rate and depth. The clot is the problem, not shallow breaths.
Alveolar fluid is pulmonary edema. PE often has normal sounds.

q: Carbon monoxide poisoning. What does this recap say about the pulse ox?

opts.why: The probe sees hemoglobin occupied and cannot tell carbon monoxide from oxygen. SpO₂ can look normal. Still give high-flow oxygen.
Pulse ox can read normal or high in carbon monoxide. It lies.
The recap’s lie is a normal or high reading, not a low one, and you still give high-flow oxygen.
The probe cannot tell carbon monoxide from oxygen.

q: Panic hyperventilation. What does this recap say not to do?

opts.t: Do not use a paper bag
opts.why: Do not have them breathe into a paper bag. It restricts oxygen. Coach slow breathing after a full assessment.
Coaching slow breathing is what you do. The recap’s don’t is the paper bag.
Box breathing is the recap’s coaching tool. The don’t is the paper bag.
Oxygen is okay if you are not sure. The recap’s don’t is the paper bag.

q: Crackles in this recap mean fluid where?

opts.why: Crackles are popping from fluid in the alveoli (pulmonary edema). Pleural effusion is fluid around the lung, so no crackles.
Fluid around the lung is pleural effusion and does not make crackles.
Upper fluid is gurgling, not crackles.
Mucus in larger airways is rhonchi. Crackles are fluid in the alveoli.

q: After albuterol, heart rate goes up. What does this recap want you to call that?

opts.why: Albuterol is a beta-2 agonist that also hits beta-1, so heart rate, palpitations, and shakiness go up. That is not shock.
Do not over-call shock when the pulse rises after albuterol.
Jitter and a faster pulse are expected side effects, not a toxic-dose name.
A faster pulse after albuterol is a drug effect, not hypovolemic shock.

q: Who is the classic spontaneous pneumothorax patient in this recap?

opts.why: Air leak without trauma. Often a tall, thin male smoker, sometimes after a hard cough. Sudden sharp pleuritic pain.
The recap’s classic is tall, thin, male, and a smoker.
This recap’s spontaneous pneumothorax is without trauma.
Barrel chest and pursed lips are emphysema in this recap, not the spontaneous pneumothorax classic.
